newsitem.title: USA: RadiSys sued by former employee - Barron's.
newsitem.headline: RadiSys sued by former employee - Barron's.

text.p: RadiSys Corp has been charged by a former employee with misrepresentation of its financial records, said Alan Abelson in his Up & Down Wall Street column in the November 25 issue of Barron's.

Abelson said that a copy of a complaint filed in Washington County Circuit Court by former RadiSys officer Bruce Taylor was obtained by Barron's and it stated that Taylor was dismissed because he discovered "significant discrepancy" in RadiSys's financial records.

Taylor, who was vice president of operations, claims in his filing that RadiSys, by misreporting inventory, overstated its earnings both before and after its public offering in order to maintain the value of its stock.

Abelson said that before Barron's obtained a copy of the complaint, it had asked the company about Taylor's litigation and had been told that it was just a wrongful-termination suit filed by an ex-employee.

A small part of the suit did deal with alleged accounting improprieties, a RadiSys spokesman said, but told Barron's that Taylor had not been involved in the company's accounting and that the complaint was "completely groundless"
Abelson said that Taylor plans to file an amended complaint, and had alerted the SEC, who started an informal probe.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
